spec.assertion: Self maxHpFlat buffApply count is >1 and <40 over 180 s. Fails under the nearest-wrong passive/always-on reading (exactly 1 application, at t=0) and under a shotFired reading (thousands). Trigger identity per taxonomy 3: an explicit attack-count clause is hitCount, counting rounds, and hitsPerShot is 1 for this MG.

Doubling the authored buff value exactly doubles the flat-resolved emitted value (caster-scaled Max HP, emitted under stat maxHpFlat), and leaves every unit total byte-identical. Fails if the line was routed through an ATK-ish stat, or if the value is hardcoded rather than read from the override. Also asserts no teammate receives Max HP from soda (target-set question: Affects self).

buffApply carries maxStacks 5 and observed stacks never exceed 5. Fails under an uncapped or wrong-cap encoding. Note: whether 5 stacks is ever ACHIEVED is cadence-dependent (180 rounds inside a rolling 10 s window needs ~18+ rounds/sec sustained, which MG wind-up and reloads interrupt) — deliberately not asserted, because a genuine non-achievement is a real engine outcome, not an override defect.

durationShots is undefined (taxonomy 2: seconds, not a round count), expiresFrame strictly advances across applications, and the last expiry sits within fight length + 600 frames. Fails under a permanent/whole-fight encoding (constant, far-future expiry) and under a for-N-rounds encoding.

⚑ The line carries NO activation clause, so its trigger is outside the input domain: the interval convention (datamined skill cooldown, first fire at t=CD) is the sanctioned default but the cadence is not in the kit text and must be flagged with the datamined value. Behavioural test only asserts the heal reaches a consumer: deleting all of skill2 must change the run (crown carries an on-recovery block). Fails if the heal is missing, or wired to a target/trigger nothing consumes.

Every heal-bearing block targets allies with excludeSelf falsy. Fails under a self-only or top-ATK-subset mis-scope; soda herself must remain a heal recipient (she is Fire and her own on-recovery consumers, if any, would depend on it).

spec.kitLine: Activates when Maid Spirit is at max
spec.assertion: There is no gate that reads a buff stack count directly, so the faithful encodings are a mirrored resource pool with resourceGate min 5, or an everyN 5 proxy on the same 180-attack trigger. The test asserts two heal blocks exist and at least one carries a condition (gate or a distinct trigger) the other does not. Fails under the nearest-wrong reading where the 12.71% heal fires unconditionally on the same cadence as the 3.23% one, which over-credits every on-recovery consumer. Residual gap: a resource pool does not decay when the Maid Spirit stacks lapse after 10 s, so a resourceGate encoding latches once reached — flagged, not asserted.

Exactly one damage bucket disappears from her event stream when the burst damage effect is stripped, and her total drops. Fails if the hit is missing, or if it is booked into the normal-attack bucket instead of the burst bucket.

Every burst-bucket damage instance has fbMajorApplied false, per the verified fact that burst-cast damage lands before Full Burst begins. Fails under the nearest-wrong fullBurstEnter keying, which would add the +50% major to the whole line.

⚑ Against the single-target scope-lock boss, 2 random enemies collapses to either 1 or 2 instances on the same target; the kit text does not decide it and damage events carry no frame field to group instances per cast. Left as it.skip so the override note is forced to state which reading it took; a silent 2x doubles the whole burst line.
it.skip. The stun primitive stops a NIKKE firing/charging/reloading; enemy targets resolve to an empty set, so a boss stun has no representation and no observable. Belongs in unmodeled.burst.

it.skip. No effect kind raises the stack count of an already-applied buff (maxStacks is per-buff and static), so the line cannot be modeled without a new primitive. Note the self-interaction it would have: soda is Fire Code, so the intended beneficiary in a mono-team is largely her own Maid Spirit (6 effective stacks). Belongs in unmodeled.burst; the override-shape group asserts at least one unmodeled.burst entry exists so this and the stun cannot both be dropped silently.

fixtures: Two, both built from controlComp('soda', true) = liter B1 / crown B2 / soda / helm B3 against the Fire boss, deterministic (no seed), 5 hoisted 180 s runs total. (1) CONTROL, used for S1 and S2: crown carries an on-recovery block, which is the only channel that makes soda amount-less heals observable, and liter/crown ally buffs let the test resolve soda slot index at runtime instead of hardcoding it. (2) BURST FIXTURE: soda is Burst I and controlComp already seats liter (also B1, earlier slot) so soda never casts her own burst in the control comp and every burst assertion there would be vacuous — the burst group appends an in-memory burstEligibility stage-3 block so she takes the B3 slot ahead of helm and actually casts. Both burst runs carry that same added block, so all burst comparisons are within-fixture and the added block cannot flatter the result. Counterfactuals are all built with withPatchedOverride and mutate the slot block arrays IN PLACE, so the test works whether a loaded slot is a raw Block[] or a CharacterSkills carrying .blocks.
gaps: it.skip — ⚑ 'Affects 2 enemy unit(s) randomly' against a single-target boss: 1 vs 2 instances per cast is an authoring choice the kit text does not decide, and damage events carry no frame field to group instances per cast; the override note must state the reading.
it.skip — GAP: 'Stun for 1 sec' has no enemy entity to land on (enemy targets resolve to an empty set), so no observable exists.
it.skip — GAP: 'Stack count of buffs ▲ 1' for Fire Code allies has no engine primitive (no effect increments an existing buff stack count).

NOT asserted (deliberate): that Maid Spirit ever REACHES 5 stacks. 180 rounds inside a rolling 10 s window needs ~18+ sustained rounds/sec, which MG wind-up and the 171-frame reload interrupt — a genuine non-achievement is an engine/cadence outcome, not an override defect, so the max-stack heal gate may be legitimately closed for most of the fight.
NOT asserted (flagged): a resourceGate encoding of the max-stack heal latches permanently once the pool reaches 5, because resource pools do not decay when the 10 s Maid Spirit stacks lapse.
